formula: hallucination_ratio = unsupported_claims / total_claims, in [0, 1]; a draft with no claims scores 0.0 (deterministic empty, D-F8-01), so the count of such cells must be reported alongside it
unsupported_claim_rule: A drafted claim is unsupported unless it is bound to a non-empty set of admitted material ids. Each result-like numeric sentence matched by SectionValidator.RESULT_NUMBER_PATTERNS counts as one additional unsupported claim, because an evaluation draft must stay planned-only.
notes: One primary metric only (karpathy constraint 1): hallucination_ratio.
The corpus and this definition are frozen together; changing either needs a new version.

hallucination_ratio covers scored cells (completed + blocked). accepted_hallucination_ratio covers ACCEPTED cells only: a non-accepted cell released no content, so it is excluded rather than counted as 0.0 -- counting it would make the score rise the more the mechanism blocks. A condition that accepted nothing reports null, never a perfect score. (Changed in 1.1; 1.0 zeroed a non-accepted cell, which let a live run with acceptance_rate 0.0 report score 100.0.)
A rate whose denominator is empty is null, not 100.0: "there was nothing to block" is not "blocking was perfect".
Unsupported claims are computed against the corpus label binding, so a condition that never retrieves material can never look well bound.
